_read: What the reviewer reads, in English. The fallback language: a key missing everywhere else
NOT here: logs (English, always, and not translated — a log is evidence, and evidence that
changes wording by locale cannot be grepped) and boot errors (a service that refuses to start
has no session and no chosen language yet).
`{name}` is replaced at render time. Keep the placeholder name, translate around it.
`language.name` is the one key that is NOT translated: it carries the language's own name, so
es.json says "Español" and never "Spanish". That is what the selector shows, and it is why
adding a fourth language is still one file — the selector reads the name out of the dictionary
instead of a list someone has to remember to edit.

people.agents.confirm.revoke: Revoke the agent token of {email}? The agent stops being able to write at once.
people.agents.heading: Agents
people.agents.lede: An agent writes through its own token: it may comment, ask and move the requests it applies, and never decides, approves or locks. A token lasts until it is revoked; issuing a new one for the same address revokes the old.
people.agents.once: The agent token for {email} is shown this once. Copy it now and give it to the agent as HOLDRIM_AGENT_TOKEN; any token this address held before has stopped working.
people.confirm.disable: Take away the access of {email}? Their approvals stay, signed with their name.
people.confirm.reset: Generate a new password for {email}? The current one stops working now, and so does every open session on the account — yours too, if this is you.
people.create.heading: Give someone access
people.lede: Who can sign in. Nobody is ever deleted: an access is taken away, and every approval they gave keeps their name.
people.name: Name
people.noAnswer: The server did not answer. Nothing was changed; try again.
people.once: The password for {email} is shown this once. Copy it now and hand it over yourself; they choose their own at first sign-in.
people.onceNew: The list shows them from the next time this page loads.

people.warn.sessionsNotDropped: The old sessions for {email} could not be confirmed closed; they may still be signed in. Do not re-enable the account to retry — that brings them back. Use {action} instead; it drops them again.
people.warn.sessionsNotDropped.reset: The old sessions for {email} could not be confirmed closed; they may still be signed in. Reset the password again to drop them.
settings.title: Settings
settings.lede: Who holds what in this deployment, and where each answer comes from. What the deployment decides is shown, with what to set and where; the project's own roles are the owner's to define and grant, here.
settings.roles.heading: Roles
settings.roles.lede: The roles this version ships, and the capabilities each one holds. A project combines capabilities; it cannot invent one.
settings.roles.lockNever: lock turns a ✓ into the one the repository trusts, and it is never granted: no role holds it, whatever the table above says of anyone. The owner holds it for being the owner, and only the deployment could ever name someone else.
settings.roles.agents: An agent never holds these, whatever else it is granted: {capabilities}.
settings.capability.read: see the documentation and its lights
settings.capability.comment: leave a remark that asks for nothing
settings.capability.request: ask for a change, and add to their own request
settings.capability.triage: decide a request: approve it, reject it, ask its author
settings.capability.approve: give a ✓ to a block, recorded as theirs and never a lock
settings.capability.lock: turn a ✓ into the one the repository trusts
settings.capability.people: create accesses, hand out passwords, disable and re-enable them
settings.holders.heading: Who holds what, and where it comes from
settings.holders.lede: Each of these is read from the environment when the service starts, and from nowhere else. To change one, change the variable where Holdrim runs, and restart it.
settings.holders.lockNotRead: Not in force yet: today a ✓ becomes a lock only when the owner gives it. HOLDRIM_LOCKS is checked at start, and the accounts it names are guarded like the owner's, but no ✓ from them is a lock until the rule on how their session was opened is built.
settings.compose.heading: Compose a lock grant
settings.compose.lede: An address and a scope: a page (P03), a page family (P0*) or a block (P03.2.1). This writes nothing. It answers with the line to set where Holdrim runs.
settings.compose.result: Set this where Holdrim runs, in place of the HOLDRIM_LOCKS it has now:
settings.compose.restart: HOLDRIM_LOCKS is read at start: nothing changes until the service restarts with it.
settings.compose.error.scope: That scope is none of a page (P03), a page family (P0*) or a block (P03.2.1).
settings.compose.error.characters: That address has characters the HOLDRIM_LOCKS line cannot carry safely. It may use letters, digits and . _ % + - before the @, and letters, digits, . and - after it.
settings.compose.error.quote: The HOLDRIM_LOCKS set now holds an address with a single quote, which this line cannot carry. Set that variable by hand.
settings.compose.error.email: That is not an address HOLDRIM_LOCKS accepts.
settings.compose.error.nothing: The scope {scope} reaches no page and no block of this site, and the service refuses to start with one that does not.
settings.compose.error.agent: HOLDRIM_AGENTS marks {email} as an agent, and the service refuses to start with a grant that names one.
settings.project.heading: What the project decides
settings.project.lede: Read from holdrim.json, in the repository. These decide what is switched on and how a person appears, never who may do what.
settings.project.snippet: To change them, commit this to holdrim.json with the values you want:
settings.projectRoles.heading: The project's roles
settings.projectRoles.lede: A role of this project: a name, and the capabilities it holds. Defining a name again redefines it in place: every grant of it holds the new capabilities from their next page or action on, and every earlier definition stays in the trail.
settings.projectRoles.name: Name
settings.projectRoles.nameHint: Lower-case words of letters, digits and -, at most {max} characters. owner, admin and member are the engine's own.
settings.projectRoles.never: A project role never holds lock or people: who may lock is the deployment's to name, and people would let a grantee hand out the very accounts other grants trust.
settings.grants.heading: Grants
settings.grants.lede: A grant gives one person one role, everywhere or within one scope, from their next page or action on. Revoking records a later event, and nothing is erased. The owner, the admins and the agents are never granted a role. Every grant is listed on the page _roles, for anyone signed in.
settings.grants.ignored: Ignored: this address is an agent.
settings.grants.scopeHint: A page (P03), a page family (P0*) or a block (P03.2.1). Empty means everywhere.
settings.grants.defineFirst: Define a role above before granting one.
settings.grants.ended: Revoked: {count}, all still in the trail.
settings.remove.heading: Remove a person
settings.remove.lede: At the person's request (docs/PRIVACY.md, section 5). Their account loses its e-mail, name, password and sessions; every comment, request and reply they wrote loses its text; their grants are revoked; and their e-mail is emptied from the people table. The trail keeps what they did, under an id that no longer leads to them: every ✓ stays as it was given, a lock included, and every snapshot stays. It cannot be undone.
settings.remove.proxy: People here sign in through an identity proxy: take the address out of the proxy first. Until then, their next visit makes them a new person.
settings.remove.email: E-mail of the person to remove
settings.remove.confirm: The person asked for this, and I understand it cannot be undone
settings.remove.done: The person was removed. The trail names them by an id from now on.
settings.remove.left: Some of their texts could not be removed ({count}): they read as tampered with, or are held inside events written before texts moved out of events. docs/PRIVACY.md lists what Holdrim cannot remove.
settings.remove.legacy: Events written before authors were ids still name this address ({count}), and nothing rewrites an event. Under password sign-in the address stays taken, so nobody new becomes their author.
